b7876ebe9513b411.text: {"thought": "Without fatigue the project is still 10.5 weeks late, so rework matters far more. I have one failure with two faces and a clear answer on rework.", "answer": "One failure, in the minimum task time of the Doing Work protection: at 0 the run stops in week 58.25 with 0 / 0 in Accomplishing, and at 0.05 week, shorter than the time step of 0.125, work is not conserved, Work to do is clipped in week 58.5 and the finish moves to week 65.5 (70.06 with half the time step). At the base settings the time step does not matter (week 70.75 against 70.69), and a normal quality of 0 behaves. Rework causes most of the delay: without it the project finishes in week 51.0, 1 week late, against 10.5 weeks late without fatigue. A guard such as MAX(Minimum_task_time, DT) in Accomplishing would remove the failure."}
b7876ebe9513b411.how: written for the book with claude-opus-5-5 (no live API call)

7675a1be6f2a95f0.text: The project is running late because work done in a hurry is often done wrong, and the flaws surface only weeks after the work has been reported done. As it is managed now, it finishes in about week 71 and costs about 2,380 person-weeks. The package (more testing from the start, 10 extra people in week 0, no overtime and an honest deadline) will deliver the system in week 62 with about 26% less effort. It beat the present approach on both time and cost in 100% of the 200 plausible worlds we simulated. Banning overtime alone is the cheapest single change that still delivers sooner, at about 1,710 person-weeks.
